- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for low sentiment.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 30d forecast peaks > true outcome peaks); apply smoothing or lagged decay to prevent overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 30d values sharply drop after peak), reduce forecast for next 5–7 days by 15–25%.
- For 30d horizon, model often fails to capture long-term trend; align forecast with 18d history weighted average if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model tends to overfit short-term swings; dampen forecast volatility by 20–30%.
- When true outcome exceeds 3x historical mean, model often fails to adjust; apply upward bias correction only if sentiment is sustained positive.
